Vitest with jsdom and Testing Library
New requirements get new IDs and tests.
Without either, database tests are skipped.
no page is tested end to end in a browser
other pages have no web tests
HMS-9 REQ-10: nextSevenDays in a PATCH body is ignored
Trade-off: a separate file keeps its own database, so the counts are not disturbed by other tests.

findings.suggested_fix: Remove the per-file database claim, or cite the harness line that proves it. Otherwise, rely on per-patient fixtures so other tests cannot change the counts.
findings.text: The trade-off says a separate test file keeps its own database. The test strategy does not say the database is isolated per file; it only says the harness starts a temporary cluster or uses HMS_TEST_DATABASE_URL.

rubric_items.reason: All 14 criteria (S-1 AC1-AC5, S-2 AC1-AC4, S-3 AC1-AC5) have at least one test that matches the criterion's given and then. No test claims a criterion that does not exist.
Counting rules are tested as API integration tests and rendering as jsdom unit tests. The only manual test is TP-17, a layout check, and it is justified by the project's lack of browser tests.

Each changed endpoint has a negative test: 404 for GET and PATCH, 400 for POST. There is a key-set boundary test (TP-21), a PATCH response check (TP-22) and a test that visitSummary in a PATCH body is ignored (TP-23).

Uses the strategy's tools (Vitest, Supertest, fixed clock, jsdom, Testing Library) and the HMS-5 REQ-n name prefix. The target files api/test/patients-visit-summary.test.ts and web/src/__tests__/PatientDetailPage.test.tsx follow existing names.
Titles give concrete data and expected values. TP-4 now names its fixed clock date (1 March 2025). The endpoint regression tests are clearly marked as such in the body.
